title: REPL Codex turn inherits ENGRAM_* from the TermAl process environment
outcome: src/turns.rs run_codex_turn spawns its own one-shot Codex app-server (per-cwd 'repl' CODEX_HOME) without clearing inherited ENGRAM_HOME/ENGRAM_ACTOR_ID/ENGRAM_SESSION_ID, so a TermAl process that itself carries an Engram identity (operator smoke test, shell launched from an Engram-enabled session) leaks that identity into the REPL agent's shell. The interactive path already scrubs the shared app-server at spawn and supplies exact per-thread values via shell_environment_policy.set; REPL mode should apply the same scrub (and, if REPL ever becomes Engram-eligible, the same thread-scoped injection). Found by the Claude reviewer during the tm-kxku.1 final review; outside that changeset's 12-file ownership, so tracked separately. Acceptance: REPL Codex child environment has none of the three variables unless explicitly injected; test on Windows and Unix; normal gates.
